title: The Classical Verbal System, Mood Governance & Morphological Stems

chapters.title: The Imperfect Tense (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Marfūʿ)
chapters.classicalFocus: Imperfect prefix and suffix paradigms; indicative markers (ḍammah or retained nūn in al-afʿāl al-khamsah); negation with mā (past) vs. lā (present).
coreRules: Indicative singular sound stems end in -u; the five dual/plural forms (afʿāl al-khamsah) retain final nūn.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 25–26: imperfect conjugation and negation.

chapters.title: The Subjunctive Mood (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Manṣūb)
chapters.textbookTitle: Moods of the Imperfect. The subjunctive
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 34 (Moods of the Verb: Indicative and Subjunctive)
chapters.classicalFocus: Subjunctive triggers (an, lan, kay, li-, ḥattā); absolute future negation with lan.
coreRules: Subjunctive marks singular stems with fatḥah and deletes final nūn (ḥadhf al-nūn) in duals and plurals.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 27–28: translating clauses of purpose and parsing lan and an clauses.

chapters.title: The Jussive Mood (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Majzūm)
chapters.textbookTitle: Moods of the Imperfect. The Jussive
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 35 (Moods of the Verb: Jussive and Imperative)
chapters.classicalFocus: Jussive governed by lam (past negation), lā al-nāhiyah (prohibition), and conditional particles.
coreRules: Jussive marks sound singulars with sukūn, drops final nūn, and apocopates final weak consonants.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 29–30: contrasting mā + past vs. lam + jussive and prohibitions.

chapters.title: The Imperative (Fiʿl al-Amr)
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 35 (Moods of the Verb: Imperative)
chapters.classicalFocus: Derivation from the jussive base; prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl prefix and its vowelling.
coreRules: Prosthetic hamzat al-waṣl takes ḍammah if the middle radical vowel is u, and kasrah if it is a or i.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 31–32: constructing positive commands and negative prohibitions.

chapters.title: The Internal Passive (Al-Fiʿl al-Majhūl)
chapters.classicalFocus: Internal vowel shifts (past fuʿila, imperfect yufʿalu); promotion of direct object to deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil).
coreRules: The agent is deleted and the deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil) takes the nominative case (rafʿ).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 33–34: converting active sentences to passive.

weeks.title: Derived Verb Stems — Principles & Forms II, III, IV

chapters.title: Morphological Principles of Augmentation (Al-Mazīd)
chapters.textbookTitle: Derived Forms of the Triliteral Verb. General Introduction
chapters.classicalFocus: Systematic root augmentation (al-mazīd) and predictable active (mu- -i-) and passive (mu- -a-) participles.
coreRules: Prefixation, infixation, and consonant doubling systematically modify core root semantics.
chapters.practiceFocus: Mapping the derived triliteral paradigm across Forms II–X.

chapters.title: Forms II, III, and IV
chapters.textbookTitle: Derived Forms of the Triliteral Verb, II, III, and IV
chapters.classicalFocus: Form II (faʿʿala, maṣdar tafʿīl), Form III (fāʿala, maṣdar mufāʿalah/fiʿāl), and Form IV (afʿala, maṣdar ifʿāl).
coreRules: Forms II, III, and IV take ḍammah on their imperfect prefixes (yu-).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 35–36: deriving Forms II–IV and analyzing causative/transitive verbs.

weeks.title: Reflexive & Reciprocal Stems — Forms V & VI

chapters.title: Forms V (tafaʿʿala) & VI (tafāʿala)
chapters.classicalFocus: Form V reflexive/resultative (maṣdar tafaʿʿul) and Form VI mutual/reciprocal (maṣdar tafāʿul); transitivity shifts.
coreRules: Prefixing ta- to Forms II and III shifts transitive verbs toward reflexive or reciprocal meanings.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 37–38: identifying theological and spiritual vocabulary in Forms V and VI.

weeks.title: Passive-Reflexive & Participatory Stems — Forms VII & VIII

chapters.title: Forms VII (infaʿala) & VIII (iftaʿala)
chapters.classicalFocus: Medio-passive Form VII (infiʿāl) and participatory Form VIII (iftiʿāl); Form VIII dental assimilation phonotactics.
coreRules: Form VIII infixed -t- assimilates after emphatics (ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ, ẓāʾ), dentals (dāl, dhāl, zāy), or wāw (e.g., ittaqā from w-q-y).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 39–40: unravelling assimilated Form VIII roots.

weeks.title: Stative & Inchoative Stems (Forms IX, X) & Doubled Verbs

chapters.title: Forms IX (ifʿalla) & X (istafʿala)
chapters.classicalFocus: Form IX (colors, bodily defects, stative conditions) and Form X (requesting, seeking, or deeming; maṣdar istifʿāl).
coreRules: Form X prefixes ista- to express seeking or considering (e.g., istaghfara: to seek forgiveness).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 41–42: invocations and petitions in Form X.

chapters.title: Doubled / Geminate Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Muḍāʿaf)
chapters.classicalFocus: Identical 2nd and 3rd radicals (madda, radda); phonotactic rules of idghām contraction vs. uncontracted stems.
coreRules: Identical radicals contract with shaddah when vowelled and separate before consonant-initial suffixes (madad-tu).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 43–44: conjugating doubled verbs across past, present, and jussive.

chapters.title: Hamzated Verbs I — Initial Hamza
chapters.textbookTitle: Hamzated Verbs. Hamza as Initial Radical
chapters.classicalFocus: Verbs with initial hamza (akhadha, akala) and irregular contracted imperatives (khudh, kul, mur).
coreRules: Common initial-hamza verbs drop the hamza in the imperative (khudh, kul, mur).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 45–46: conjugating initial-hamza verbs.

chapters.title: Hamzated Verbs II — Middle & Final Hamza
chapters.textbookTitle: Hamza as Middle and Final Radical
chapters.classicalFocus: Medial/final hamza (saʾala, qaraʾa) and orthographic seat rules (alif, wāw, yāʾ, or on the line).
coreRules: Hamza seat selection follows the vowel-strength hierarchy: kasrah > ḍammah > fatḥah > sukūn.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 47–48: writing hamza accurately across varying declensions.

chapters.title: Assimilated Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Mithāl)
chapters.classicalFocus: Initial weak radical wāw or yāʾ (waṣala, waqaʿa); systematic elision of initial wāw in Form I imperfect and imperative.
coreRules: Initial wāw drops in Form I imperfects with middle kasrah (yaṣilu) and in the imperative (ṣil).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 49–50: tracking wāw elision in prayer and scripture.

chapters.title: Hollow Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Ajwaf)
chapters.classicalFocus: Middle radical wāw or yāʾ (qāla, bāʿa, khāfa); morphophonemic vowel shortening in closed syllables.
coreRules: When the third radical takes sukūn (qultu, lam yaqul), the long medial vowel shortens.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 51–52: hollow verbs across all three moods.

chapters.title: Defective Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Nāqiṣ)
chapters.textbookTitle: The Verb with Weak Final Radical
chapters.classicalFocus: Final radical wāw or yāʾ (daʿā, ramā, raḍiya); jussive/imperative apocopation; defective nouns and participles (al-qāḍī / qāḍin).
coreRules: In the jussive and imperative, the final weak letter is deleted completely (lam yadʿu, lam yarmi).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 53–54: conjugating defective verbs across moods.

chapters.title: Root-Based Lexicography & Dictionary Mechanics
chapters.textbookTitle: How to Use an Arabic Dictionary
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Appendix I (How to Use an Arabic Dictionary)
chapters.classicalFocus: Identifying roots, stripping augmented affixes (ḥurūf al-ziyādah), and navigating classical dictionaries (Hans Wehr, Lane's Lexicon).
coreRules: Restore weak and assimilated radicals to their underlying triliteral root before dictionary lookup.
chapters.practiceFocus: Dictionary lookup drills of classical roots.

weeks.title: Multiply Weak Verbs, Quadriliterals & Consolidation of Module 2

chapters.title: Doubly & Trebly Weak Verbs (Al-Lafīf)
chapters.textbookTitle: The Doubly and Trebly Weak Verb
chapters.classicalFocus: Doubly and trebly weak verbs (al-lafīf al-maqrūn and al-mafrūq, e.g., ḥayiya, waqā, raʾā) and minimal imperative stems (qi).
coreRules: Doubly weak verbs combine initial/medial weak rules with defective final-radical deletion.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 55–56: conjugating doubly weak verbs.

chapters.title: Quadriliteral Verbs & Module 2 Consolidation
chapters.classicalFocus: Four-radical verbs (faʿlala, e.g., zalzala, waswasa) and derived forms; systematic conjugation review across all derived and weak paradigms.
coreRules: Quadriliteral verbs conjugate in parallel with Form II and Form V triliteral verbs.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 57–58: parsing Qur'anic verses featuring quadriliterals (Sūrat al-Zalzalah) and Module 2 paradigm review.
